newsitem.title: USA: Kentucky stock tax ruled illegal, refunds ordered.
newsitem.headline: Kentucky stock tax ruled illegal, refunds ordered.

text.p: The Kentucky Supreme Court ruled the state's intangibles tax law illegal and ordered it to refund up to $240 million, the Lexington Herald-Leader reported Friday.
In a ruling Thursday, the court said the tax violated laws governing interstate commerce because it taxed the stock of in-state and out-of-state companies at different rates.
Gov. Paul Patton told the newspaper that paying the refunds would be "a major problem" but that the state should be able to come up with the money.

The refund order fell short of the amount sought by taxpayers who challenged the law in a 1990 class-action lawsuit. They sought refunds dating back to 1988, which could have cost the state up to $341 million.

The court ruled that for each valid claim, refunds would be paid for two years prior. For example, a taxpayer who filed for a refund in 1993 would get refunds back to 1991. Those who file now will receive refunds for 1995 and 1996.
In addition to paying the refunds, Kentucky will also lose the $30 million in annual revenues it collected from the tax.

For companies that pay taxes in Kentucky on at least 75 percent of their property, stock held by Kentucky residents was taxed at one-tenth of a cent per $100 of assessed value, a rate so low it was rarely collected.
But stock in out-of-state companies was taxed at 25 cents per $100 of assessed value,
The U.S. Supreme Court struck down a similar law in North Carolina and several other states have repealed their intangibles taxes amid legal challenges.
